# Projects

## Health Risk Modeling Analysis

Investigated whether physical food access or socioeconomic factors better explain chronic health outcomes across Lancaster County, Nebraska. Found that educational attainment was a substantially stronger predictor of obesity than proximity to grocery stores. That result held across both linear and nonlinear models.

**Tools:** Python, pandas, scikit-learn, geopandas\
**Data:** ACS (U.S. Census Bureau), CDC PLACES, OpenStreetMap

[View Report (PDF)](files/Math_in_the_City___Group_4__Spring_2026.pdf){target="_blank"}

<details>

<summary>See technical details</summary>

- Engineered distance based and density features from OpenStreetMap using OSMnx (distance to nearest grocery store, fast food density per km²)
- Built a multiple linear regression model achieving R² ≈ 0.49. Compared against random forest (R² ≈ 0.59).
- Feature importance analysis confirmed percent without a high school diploma (importance 0.721) as the dominant predictor over physical food access (0.143)
- Performed 5 fold cross validation to evaluate model stability across tract subsets
- Visualized spatial clustering of obesity, poverty, and transit access across census tracts using geopandas

</details>

## Health Risk Modeling, Extended Analysis
 
After completing the class project, I wanted to test whether adding more policy relevant
variables would change the findings. The original analysis identified educational
attainment as the strongest predictor of obesity. Adding SNAP participation rates and
age distribution data from the ACS shifted that picture considerably.
 
**Key finding.** SNAP participation (r = 0.76) and educational attainment (r = 0.75)
emerged as essentially tied bivariate predictors of obesity. The random forest breaks
the tie: education leads with an importance weight of 0.527, more than double SNAP at
0.241. The high collinearity between the two (r = 0.71) explains this. Both variables
point to the same urban core tracts as the highest risk areas.
 
**Tools.** Python, pandas, scikit-learn, geopandas, statsmodels\
**Data.** ACS 5-year 2024, CDC PLACES 2025, OpenStreetMap, TIGER/Line 2020
 
[View Notebook](files/analysis.html){target="_blank"}
 
<details>
<summary>See technical details</summary>
- Added SNAP participation rate, percent population under 18, and percent 65+ from ACS to the original feature set
- Random forest feature importance: percent_no_hs (0.527), snap_rate (0.241), pct_under_18 (0.063). Food access variables combined below 0.05.
- Linear regression R² = 0.517. Random Forest R² = 0.609 on the held out test set. Repeated K fold CV mean R² = 0.565 (RF) vs 0.299 (LR).
- Spatial mapping shows SNAP concentration and low educational attainment overlap almost perfectly in Lancaster County's urban core
- Decision tree (max depth 4) confirmed educational attainment as the primary splitting variable
- The age split is notable. pct_65_plus negatively correlates with obesity (r = -0.45) but positively with coronary heart disease (r = 0.74), suggesting distinct drivers across outcomes.
</details>
